verdict.rationale: Cactus's core inference engine is open source and runs entirely on the user's own hardware: brew install and `cactus run`, documented local-run platforms, no server, and free local LoRA fine-tuning with the open-source package. However, the platform's hosted features (GPU training, full-model training, the trained confidence head, 2-bit exports, and data generation) are documented only as hosted API services, so the full product is not self-hostable. Missing for 10: self-hostable versions of the platform features (full-model training, confidence-head training, 2-bit export, data generation API), and independent hands-on corroboration of a full self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Step 1: brew install cactus-compute/cactus/cactus - Step 2: cactus run
Free: $0 for local LoRA fine-tuning with the open-source package. Bring your own hardware and data
macOS and Linux on Arm and x86, Windows on x64 and Arm64, Python 3.9 or newer, no GPU.
No GPU, no server, and no data leaving the device.
